notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate information disclosure flaw was found in Grafana, affecting the grafana component as shipped in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10, Red Hat Ceph Storage, Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes, Multicluster Global Hub, and Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, as well as Red Hat Hardened Images and Fedora community builds. This unintended proxying allows an attacker to read sensitive Azure cloud resources within the scope of that identity's permissions, with no impact on integrity or availability. Some RHEL 8 grafana streams are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present. Red Hat rates this flaw 4.3 (Moderate) rather than the upstream 6.3 because the disclosure is bounded by the Azure role granted to the data source identity, resulting in low confidentiality impact with unchanged scope rather than the high confidentiality impact across a changed scope assessed upstream. For the affected Red Hat products the fix is deferred to a future update given the moderate impact and the authentication and query-access prerequisites; the residual risk is that an authenticated user could retrieve Azure resources accessible to the data source identity. Axios fails to parse Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation in proxy bypass lists as IP address ranges, treating them as plain text hostnames instead. notes.text: A moderate information disclosure vulnerability was found in Axios, a promise-based HTTP client for Node.js that Red Hat Hardened Images (Hummingbird) ships as a dependency of its grafana12.4, grafana13.1, and grafana13.2 container images. Axios evaluates Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation entries in NO_PROXY proxy-bypass lists as textual hostname suffixes instead of IP address ranges. When a request targets an address covered by a CIDR entry in NO_PROXY while a proxy is configured, the CIDR bypass rule fails to match and the request is sent through the configured proxy. As a result, an adversary with access to the configured proxy server can observe and modify URLs, headers, and bodies of plaintext HTTP traffic intended for internal network services, and can observe connection metadata and CONNECT requests for HTTPS traffic. Red Hat rated this flaw as moderate severity (CVSS 6.5), consistent with the upstream assessment of moderate severity (CVSS 6.9). descriptions.value:
A file overwrite vulnerability exists in Epiphany when installing WebExtension packages from .xpi files.

In src/webextension/ephy-web-extension-manager.c, decompress_xpi_thread() used libarchive with archive_read_support_format_all() (and filters), so the installer did not require a real ZIP. A TAR file named *.xpi was extracted. TAR supports hard-link entry types; with Epiphany's archive_write_disk options (including ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_PERM), a crafted hard-link target can cause an attacker-chosen existing user-writable file to be truncated and overwritten with attacker-controlled content and mode bits, without a dedicated warning dialog, when the user installs or opens the crafted .xpi.

This is related to but separate from the ZIP-slip path traversal fixed as CVE-2026-77679 (#2922 / MR !2143).

Requirements: the victim must install or open a malicious WebExtension (.xpi).

Affected: Epiphany >= 47.0 (WebExtension XPI install path).
Fixed: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/merge_requests/2248 (commit 0cc9ab55 — only enable ZIP format support).
Upstream: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/work_items/2988
Reporter acknowledgment: Fernando Munoz

descriptions.value:
A logic error in Epiphany's site permission handling can cause camera and microphone access to be granted when the user only approves a different permission.

In src/ephy-window.c, set_permission() stores the user's Allow/Deny choice after a WebKit permission dialog. Types CLIPBOARD and WEBSITE_DATA_ACCESS are not stored by ephy_permission_is_stored_by_permissions_manager(), so control fell into an else-if that was written as:

  } else if (EPHY_PERMISSION_TYPE_ACCESS_WEBCAM_AND_MICROPHONE) {

Because that expression is a non-zero enum constant, the branch always ran for those types and wrote EPHY_PERMISSION_PERMIT for both ACCESS_WEBCAM and ACCESS_MICROPHONE for the site origin. The user only saw a Clipboard or Website Data Access dialog.

A malicious site that obtains approval for clipboard or third-party storage access can afterwards use getUserMedia without a further camera/microphone prompt, exposing audiovisual confidentiality.

Requirements: the victim must visit a malicious page and click Allow on a clipboard or website-data-access prompt.

Affected: Epiphany >= 45.0 (bug present at least through 51.x).
Fixed: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/merge_requests/2249 (commit 480c3648).
Upstream: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/work_items/2976
Reporter acknowledgment: Fernando Munoz

descriptions.value: The Germanized for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Unauthorized Access of Private Data via Activation Token Reuse in versions up to, and including, 4.1.4. This is due to the `on_user_email_changed` hook — which is responsible for rotating the activation token and recording a pending-email-change marker on an unactivated Customer account — only being registered inside the `is_double_opt_in_login_enabled()` branch when "Disable login for unactivated customers" is set to Yes, leaving the original `?activate=` token valid and entirely unbound to the email address it was issued for when that setting is No. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to change their account email to a victim's billing email via the standard `/my-account/edit-account/` form and then redeem their original activation token through `customer_account_activate()`, triggering `link_customer_past_orders()` to reassign any matching guest order to the attacker's account and exposing the original buyer's billing name, street address, phone number, and purchased items on the attacker's My Account order page. Exploitation requires the site to have double opt-in enabled with "Disable login for unactivated customers" explicitly set to No (a non-default configuration), public customer registration enabled, and the original activation token redeemed within its one-day expiry window.

descriptions.value: The FlexStock – Product Stock Sync with Google Sheets for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'products[].post_content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.17.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable by any Subscriber-level user because the plugin's admin_enqueue_scripts callback exposes the REST bearer token in the Dashboard page source via wp_localize_script() without a capability check, and the REST endpoint's permission_callback validates only that bearer token rather than performing a current_user_can() capability check.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in luksmeta. A local attacker with administrative privileges can cause data corruption when saving metadata to a Linux Unified Key Setup (LUKS) device. Due to incorrect boundary calculations and flawed overlap detection, new metadata entries can be written beyond available free space or over existing records. This issue can corrupt stored encrypted payload data or existing metadata, potentially rendering the affected data inaccessible.
